transcript:
Header:
Date/Time: 2026-04-16 14:00 UTC | Duration: 55m
Attendees: Alex (Redwood AE), Priya (Redwood SE), Jordan (Redwood CSM) — Sam, Lina, Marcus, Tessa (Northfield)

Summary:
Quick commercial handoff between AE/SE and Northfield procurement/legal; focus on MSA/DPA redlines, pricing for a 3-month pilot, Dedicated vs hosted SLAs, and KMS keying/egress obligations. Action items and next steps captured at end.

Topics:
- MSA redline priorities (data residency, indemnity)
- DPA scoping for PII and retention windows
- SLA thresholds, latency SLOs, uptime and rollback policies
- Pricing: pilot discount, burst capacity, egress fees
- KMS/HSM and SSO/SAML integration, RBAC

Transcript: 
[00:00] Alex: hey everyone, thanks for joining. we wanted to run through the commercial bits and the security asks so we can hand off to legal and procurement, um, quick check - did you get the draft MSA?
[00:10] Sam: yes we did, thanks. Lina had a few flag points, mostly around section 5, um, liability caps, and the data residency table didn't exactly match our region list.
[00:18] Lina: yeah the DPA's okay but we need an option to scope out certain PII types and a shorter retention window for logs, we also want clear audit log retention and whether you keep redwood console traces for longer than 90 days.
[00:30] Jordan: note, console tracing retention is configurable on Redwood Console, you can set per-route retention; i'll attach the doc - apologies if i said Redwoood Console in the deck, that's a typo in slide 4.
[00:40] Marcus: on the infra side, we need to confirm KMS flow - we use AWS KMS with external key wrap; can you support bring-your-own-key, HSM backed, and key rotation?
[00:50] Priya: yes BYOK is supported for Private deployments, and Dedicated can integrate with customer KMS via a gateway. rotation policies we can align to your cadence, though for Hosted we'll be managing keys unless you opt for our customer-managed keystore path.
[01:05] Tessa: is that the path where the key never leaves customer control? we need an HSM-backed assurance - also we are under a fedramp-ish audit later this year, so we need to describe control mappings.
[01:18] Alex: understood, we'll surface our control mappings and the SOC2 report. Jordan will share the encryption whitepaper that shows the HSM/BYOK flow.
[01:26] Sam: pricing - the procurement team wants a 3-month pilot with a capped spend and burst capacity, can you do a pilot rate card? also curious on egress charges if we test model exports.
[01:40] Priya: for pilots we typically do a reduced per-token rate and a fixed monthly cap; burst capacity for Dedicated is possible but we'd need an agreement on burstable slots and a higher temporary commit. egress: exports of model artifacts are chargeable per GB; inference token egress is part of usage but data transfer out of regions could have fees.
[01:57] Marcus: please call out whether KV cache and prefix caching count toward token usage; we need to size correctly.
[02:05] Priya: KV cache hits reduce compute; the billing is based on tokens generated plus model compute time but cache hits do reduce the effective tokens billed. i'll send a worked example.
[02:15] Lina: indemnity and liability cap - we prefer a higher cap for regulated data, and a clause for regulatory subpoenas. is Redwood open to scoped liability for PII mishandling?
[02:30] Alex: we can discuss a tiered cap tied to committed spend; i'll flag commercial with finance, but legal may push back on unlimited liability.
[02:37] Sam: and SSO - we use SAML 2.0 with SCIM for provisioning. we need RBAC sync with our identity provider for roles and least privilege.
[02:47] Jordan: Redwood supports SAML SSO and SCIM for provision; RBAC maps to roles in Console, and we offer private deployments that can broker SSO inside your VPC for stricter network rules.
[02:58] Tessa: one more on compliance - do you capture request/response payloads in logs by default? we need ability to redact or not log specific fields.
[03:10] Priya: you can configure request logging and field redaction in the ingest pipeline; default hosted mode retains minimal metadata but for Private/Dedicated we have more controls.
[03:20] Sam: timeline - if legal signs the MSA with our redlines in 2 weeks, we want the pilot to start by May 10. what do you need to make that happen?
[03:30] Alex: we'll need final redlines, a signed SOW for pilot scope, and Priya's test run to validate latency and throughput. also agreement on pilot billing cap.
[03:40] Marcus: ok i'll prepare a minimal dataset and masked sample for Priya.
[03:44] Priya: great, i'll run tests on both Hosted and Dedicated path to show delta and share logs, expect about 48-72 hours to run the full suite once i have the sample and traffic profile.
[03:56] Lina: can you put the DPA changes into track-changes and call out any non-standard clauses so legal can review quickly?
[04:05] Jordan: yes i'll prepare a redline with notes and attach the SOC2 and KMS flow doc.
[04:12] Sam: competitors - we've also been talking to Anthropic and a smaller infra provider called CloudX Labs; their pricing is competitive but they didn't have the private deployment assurances we need.
[04:25] Alex: understood, we'll highlight the private-hosted parity and the rollback/fallback policies.
[04:32] Recap / Next Steps:
- Alex to update term sheet with egress assumptions, pilot rate and tiered liability proposal (due 2026-04-19).
- Jordan to upload SOC2, DPA redline, and KMS integration doc (due 2026-04-18).
- Priya to run Dedicated vs Hosted latency/throughput tests on masked sample (due 2026-04-23).
- Northfield to provide masked dataset and final redlines (Sam/Marcus/Lina) (target 2026-04-20).

Action Items (spoken):
- Priya: run tests, share logs.
- Alex: update commercial.
- Jordan: share compliance docs.

Close: thanks all, we'll follow up in the thread with the redlined MSA and pilot SOW.
